title: Registry status pin coverage: every capability asserted, every ACTIVE capability pinned exactly -- and the attribution instrument that can tell which family an assertion is about
objective: Close GOV-0094 with the rule the tree can actually carry. The issue's 'exactly one EXACT pin per capability' is falsified by measurement; the guard enforces two clauses instead, and ships status assertions for the three capabilities that had none.
business_value: A capability nothing asserts can regress or advance silently. Three did. The wider value is the instrument: attribution by data flow rather than co-occurrence, which two prior sweeps got wrong in opposite directions and which is reusable by any future registry guard.
in_scope: tests/test_badf_registry_status_pins.py: (a) the attribution instrument -- binds each ['status'] assertion to the family whose registry entry the subscripted expression was LOOKED UP BY, argument-order agnostic, handling tuple-packed / loop-driven / aliased-iterable / helper-call shapes; (b) clause 1, every capability carries >=1 status assertion; (c) clause 2, every ACTIVE capability carries >=1 EXACT pin; (d) the control set as tests -- BARCHI-3's four plus C5 (no false rejection), each shape a named fixture with a positive control; (e) floor assertions for badf-delivery, badf-prd and repository-research, which have no contract module of their own
work/WP-2026-0128/work-package.json: the inherited reconcile (landed 0afcb14); derived output of `badf_gate.py reconcile`, ownership mechanical
out_of_scope: The issue's original 'exactly one EXACT pin per capability'. MEASURED AND REJECTED, not deferred: it holds for 17 of 30 families and enforcing it would require deleting 20 correct pins (badf-git carries 11). Duplicate pins are several modules independently refusing to let the root drift, not a defect. Reframing accepted by the issue's author.
Changing any existing pin or floor. The issue says they are correct as they stand and the audit agrees -- 0 exact pins disagree with the registry.

A badf_gate.py `repo` control. This is a test-suite property, not a repository one; the issue named a gate control as probable over-engineering and the Lean ladder stops at the cheapest thing that works.
#268's consolidation (a pin on a surface the capability does not own). The two issues fail in opposite directions; this one is the buildable half and does not resolve the other.
Exact pins for mid-ladder families. Clause 2 is deliberately restricted to ACTIVE per BARCHI-3's refinement and the denominator rule.
change_class_rationale: One new test module plus a derived reconcile. No production code, no schema, no gate control. Reversible by reverting one squash commit.
data_classification_rationale: Test-suite and registry metadata; no credentials or personal data.
acceptance_criteria: Clause 1 red-first: with the three new assertions excised, the guard fails NAMING badf-delivery, badf-prd and repository-research.
Clause 2 green for all 8 ACTIVE families without any new exact pin -- it codifies what already holds.
The control set passes: C1 pin-moved, C2 pin-stayed-literal-first, C3 the six two-family badf-git functions, C4 non-registry rejection, C5 no false rejection of a real pin.
C5 uses a REAL pin as its must-not-reject case, never a synthetic one (BARCHI-3): a synthetic pin would be a fixture testing itself.
Each of the three shapes prior sweeps missed -- tuple-packed, loop-driven, aliased-iterable -- has a named fixture and a positive control.

The instrument is proven able to SEE floors, by reproducing the three floor tuples #218's own body names. Without this, 'no family is floor-only' is indistinguishable from 'the instrument is blind to floors'.
Mutation: each control neutered -> its own named test red, with an in-process positive control staying GREEN.
The synthetic fixture's syntheticness is CHECKED, not claimed: a test asserts badf-midladder is absent from the registry.

Open-ended adversarial clause (#270): what else reaches 'a capability whose status nothing asserts'? Walk the registry, not the examples -- the audit's own failure was a regex that sampled shapes instead of enumerating them.

test_obligations.claim: clause 1 fires naming the three unasserted capabilities; the control set including C5 passes; each missed shape has a fixture; every control dies under mutation with a positive control surviving

evidence: failing-first: clause 1 red with the three assertions excised
control set: 5/5 including the added C5
mutation: 5/5 controls killed, in-process positive control GREEN each
audit measurement published before any id was bound (comment 5489640064)
evidence_obligations: the audit numbers were measured with a gate-passing instrument, and the gate was extended (C5) when the first build passed C4 while making four false rejections
the floor-visibility control runs before any floor-derived claim is made
risk_factors: The guard scans tests/ by AST; a future pin written in a shape the instrument does not model would be invisible to clause 1 and the capability would silently lose coverage. Mitigated by the shape fixtures, not eliminated -- stated rather than hidden.
This work package creates the first three real floor-only families, which changes the premise the synthetic fixture was justified by. Recorded in the module docstring.

dependencies.note: Carries 0128's reconcile; the guard itself is independent.

rollback.method: revert the squash commit via PR
